title: Creative employment is geographically concentrated and structurally distinctive in London
source_unit: Office for National Statistics ONS Local user-requested APS extract: estimated creative-industries jobs and demographic breakdowns, 2025
geography: London versus all other regions of the United Kingdom; Annual Population Survey estimates

observations.period: 2025; estimated jobs by region; creative industries under the DCMS SIC-based definition

denominator.unit: Estimated total jobs within each regional universe; 95% confidence intervals supplied in the workbook

london_creative_share.unit: percent of estimated London jobs; derived from workbook totals

other_uk_creative_jobs.unit: estimated jobs outside London; 95% CI 1657568 to 1777446

other_uk_all_jobs.unit: estimated jobs outside London; 95% CI 28768866 to 29050272

other_uk_creative_share.unit: percent of estimated jobs outside London; derived from workbook totals

mechanism.value: Creative employment is not evenly distributed across place: London has a much larger creative-job share, making cultural production, career entry, housing pressure, local identity, and regional policy capacity jointly connected rather than separate market questions

observations.method: ONS user-requested Annual Population Survey extract using person weights PWTA22; creative industries are defined from selected SIC 2007 industries using the DCMS definition, with regional estimates and 95% confidence intervals.
observations.uncertainty: ONS warns that APS quality has been affected by low response rates, accreditation was withdrawn from official statistics based on APS, 2022-based population weights were used, and these figures are not directly comparable with other published analyses. London is compared with a broad residual region, not a full local typology.
observations.subgroup: London and all other regions of the United Kingdom; estimated total jobs.
observations.counterinterpretation: The London share may reflect industry classification, commuting and place-of-work patterns, concentration of headquarters and cultural institutions, population composition, or measurement quality rather than a simple local cultural advantage.

observations.period: 2025; creative jobs by sex and employment type

denominator.unit: Estimated creative-industry jobs in each region; subgroup totals have separate confidence intervals

london_creative_self_employed_share.unit: percent of London creative jobs; derived from workbook totals

other_uk_creative_self_employed_jobs.unit: estimated jobs outside London; 95% CI 469834 to 533294

other_uk_creative_self_employed_share.unit: percent of creative jobs outside London; derived from workbook totals

mechanism.value: Creative-sector place concentration coexists with a substantial self-employed workforce and a London sex composition of roughly 40% women and 60% men, making bargaining, income volatility, care, and local opportunity part of cultural-production capacity

observations.method: ONS APS creative-industry estimates from workbook tables 6 and 11; sex and employment-type cells are descriptive estimates with published confidence intervals.
observations.uncertainty: Sex and self-employment comparisons are not causal and may reflect occupation, industry, age, education, class, hours, earnings, household structure, and sampling uncertainty. Self-employment is not a direct measure of autonomy or precarity.
observations.subgroup: Creative-industry jobs in London and all other UK regions, by sex and employee/self-employed status.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high self-employed share may represent entrepreneurial control, contracting norms, portfolio work, or forced independence; the extract does not measure earnings, hours, job quality, or worker voice.

observations.period: 2025; creative jobs by disability and qualification

denominator.unit: Estimated creative-industry jobs in each region; disability and qualification cells have separate confidence intervals

london_creative_disabled_share.unit: percent of London creative jobs; derived from workbook totals

other_uk_creative_disabled_jobs.unit: estimated jobs outside London; 95% CI 249963 to 296147

other_uk_creative_disabled_share.unit: percent of creative jobs outside London; derived from workbook totals

london_creative_degree_jobs.unit: estimated jobs among degree-or-equivalent qualification group; 95% CI 554994 to 644252

london_creative_degree_share.unit: percent of London creative jobs; derived from workbook totals

mechanism.value: Creative opportunity is highly credentialed in London while disability representation is lower there than outside London in this estimate; the open question is whether this reflects access, occupational sorting, age and health composition, workplace accommodation, or classification

observations.method: ONS APS creative-industry estimates from workbook tables 7 and 8; disability is the published APS status and qualification is the highest qualification grouping.
observations.uncertainty: Small or subgroup estimates can have wide confidence intervals; disability and qualification are not causal mechanisms, and the APS quality warning applies. Derived shares use rounded or estimated totals and should not be read as exact workforce composition.
observations.subgroup: Creative-industry jobs in London and all other UK regions by disability status and highest qualification.
observations.counterinterpretation: The London-versus-rest difference may arise from age, migration, occupation, survey response, industry mix, or different disclosure patterns; it is not evidence of exclusion without access, hiring, retention, or accommodation measures.

DCMS creative-industries definition referenced by the ONS workbook.
Annual Population Survey context and design.

boundary: This record adds a local labor-market and demographic layer to cultural-consumer analysis. It is an ONS user-requested APS estimate with explicit quality and comparability warnings, not a causal evaluation of London cultural power, a measure of cultural consumption, an earnings or job-quality estimate, or proof of inclusion or exclusion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: ONS release page and associated creativeindustriesjobs2025.xlsx workbook reviewed; Table 1 regional totals, Tables 6-8 sex/disability/qualification, Table 11 employment type, confidence intervals, APS weighting, definition, and quality warnings preserved.
